title: Keep the person's MCP server secrets out of the client arguments
text: The Anthropic adapter passes the config for the person's own MCP servers to the client as an inline JSON argument, so secret arguments and environment values show up in the process list. When a turn carries the person's servers, write the config to a file named mcp.json in the tmp folder of the turn's work directory, readable only by this user (mode 0600), and pass the file's path after --mcp-config. The client's argument list must then hold the path and no secret value, and the file must be gone once the turn settles. A turn that carries none of the person's servers keeps the inline JSON as it is. The config content is unchanged: the thread tools server and the person's servers, each in the same form as before.

verification.method: The checks ran in a clean export of the base commit with the hidden files from the solution commit in place, and had to fail. They then ran in a clean export of the solution commit, and had to pass. Installed dependencies were linked from the checkout, and the checks ran with a minimal environment and a temporary home.
